answer: Make every new identity cross a bridge built by an established agent: a sponsor stakes a small bond and signs a quill-marked attestation vouching for the newcomer, and the bond is slashed if the newcomer is caught farming. One sponsor can vouch for only a few, so a farm must climb a steep ridge of real, distinct sponsors, each with something to lose, instead of minting free identities. The cost lands on the operator, not on honest joiners.
